title: AI Security Guide and  Risk Assessment Tool
date_source: publication landing page https://www.rand.org/pubs/tools/TLA4174-1.html — <meta name="citation_publication_date" content="2026/2/12"> and on-page "Published Feb 12, 2026". The chapter URLs carry no date of their own; they are surfaces of the one dated publication TL-A4174-1.
rule_cited: §2 — documented process fact (methodology/tooling finding), which §2 admits explicitly; §3 dedup — primary, fullest source for TL-A4174-1
reason: Close call, and I record it as such. The guide itself is prescriptive (controls and recommendations), which §2 test 2 excludes. But Appendix E documents a process RAND actually carried out — using its own GPT-4o instance as the control-to-threat mapping instrument, then validating that output by hand — and §2 admits methodology and tooling findings. RAND is a named evaluator, so §1 is satisfied. This root URL is the primary and fullest surface, so the 44 chapter URLs in this chunk fold into it.

findings.finding: RAND built the guide's control-prioritisation layer with an LLM in the loop: its internal GPT-4o instance mapped each security control to OWASP and Berryville Institute of Machine Learning threat categories, and RAND subject-matter experts then manually reviewed and validated that mapping before controls were scored by inverse OWASP criticality weighting.
findings.finding_quote: We used an internal large language model (LLM), RAND’s instance of GPT-4o, to map each security control to relevant Open Web Application Security Project (OWASP) and Berryville Institute of Machine Learning (BIML) threats.
findings.tier_reasoning: §4 Gate 1 fails: this is not an empirical model finding — no property of GPT-4o is measured; the model is the INSTRUMENT of a methodology study, which §4 names explicitly. Gate 1 "no" therefore forces TIER C with action_trackable left BLANK, per the encoding rule.
findings.scope: Development methodology of the RAND AI Security Guide (TL-A4174-1)
findings.access_type: internal enterprise deployment of a commercial model (black-box)
